summary: A partial, map-level decomposition of the weight-two comparison. Seven targets separate the corrected degree-zero cycle, its modular-quotient Kummer image, character sums, stabilization, the positive-conductor norm relation, differential evaluation, and the ordinary p-old family comparison. No completed main-conjecture export or integral cycle-lattice equivalence is claimed. A dimension obstruction to the symmetric-power/induction identification in the published Castella--Hsieh paper is recorded for independent review. Initial-conductor unit factors and the regulator conventions of different source versions remain explicit gaps.

nodes.title: The weight-two cycle is the corrected CM divisor
nodes.statement: Let C be the modular curve used by the BDP construction, L a characteristic-zero field over which the CM point x_phi and a degree-one cusp b are rational, and identify X_0 with C by the empty-fiber-power identification. The homologically trivial weight-two cycle is [x_phi]-[b] in CH^1(C_L)_Q. After applying the chosen cuspidal Hecke correspondence e_f it is e_f([x_phi]-[b]). The raw point [x_phi] has degree one and is not the input to the degree-zero Abel--Jacobi map.
hypotheses: BDP's fiber-power index is k-2, whereas CH writes the weight as 2r; weight two means respectively index 0 and r=1.
Use the actual level structure and its field of definition. A ring class field alone is not asserted to define every chosen level point or cusp.
The empty fiber-power identification and the action of e_f are the constructions supplied by GH.0--GH.1, not new abstract carriers.
proofSteps: Compute the zeroth graph product in the fiber above x_phi and carry it through X_0=C.
Subtract the chosen cusp and compute its degree as 1-1. For a smooth proper curve, the degree-zero divisor class has zero geometric degree-two cycle class.
Apply the already constructed correspondence to this divisor class; do not apply the positive-fiber-power vanishing argument at index zero.
acceptance: x_phi=b gives zero, whereas retaining [x_phi] gives degree one.
Changing b to b' changes the class by [b]-[b']; this is an identity, not an integral assertion of independence.
Test the weight dictionary k=2 against both source indices and retain any extension needed to define the level structure.

sources.locator: Section 2.3, Proposition 2.7 and preceding paragraph, printed p. 1063
sources.match: The preceding paragraph supplies the index-zero cusp correction; the proposition is the homological-triviality statement. This node isolates that special case.

nodes.title: Abel--Jacobi and Kummer classes under the modular quotient
nodes.statement: For the preceding C, x_phi, b and L, let J=Pic^0(C), let pi:C->E be the chosen modular parametrization defined over L, and let q_pi:J->E satisfy q_pi([x]-[b])=pi(x)-pi(b). Let theta_C:V_p J -> H^1_et(C_bar,Q_p(1)) be the Picard--Kummer identification. With the corresponding f-projector on J satisfying q_pi e_f=q_pi, set gamma_pi=V_p(q_pi) composed with theta_C^{-1}. Then H^1(L,gamma_pi)(AJ_et(e_f([x_phi]-[b]))) equals kappa_E(pi(x_phi)-pi(b)) in H^1_cont(L,V_p E). Both sides may be extended to the same finite coefficient field. This is a rational-coefficient statement; it does not identify two chosen integral lattices.
hypotheses: C is smooth, proper and geometrically connected, L has characteristic zero, and p is prime.
The degree-one Abel--Jacobi construction uses the cycle class and Hochschild--Serre/Gysin convention of GH.1; the connecting cocycle is sigma(Q)-Q.
The Picard--Kummer identification and the correspondence action must be proved compatible with that convention; their concrete contract is the GH.1 request below.
The morphism q_pi and q_pi e_f=q_pi come from the actual modular quotient. They are not inferred from equality of dimensions or equality of Hecke eigenvalues alone.
proofSteps: Use the finite-level Picard--Kummer/Gysin comparison to identify the degree-one Abel--Jacobi class of D with theta_C applied to the Kummer class of [D] in J. This finite-level comparison, including its sign, is explicitly requested from GH.1.
At p^n choose a division point Q of [D]. Applying q_pi sends its connecting cocycle sigma(Q)-Q to the connecting cocycle of q_pi([D]); changing Q changes both by the corresponding coboundary.
Use compatible p-power division points and the actual continuous-cochain/adic realization comparison to pass to V_p. Do not commute H^1 with inverse limits without that comparison.
Apply q_pi e_f=q_pi and the divisor description of the previous node. This gives the displayed equality and fixes the basepoint translation.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve C with its origin as b and pi the identity, recover the ordinary rational Kummer class of x_phi.
Replacing b by b' changes the image by kappa_E(pi(b)-pi(b')).
A torsion basepoint difference vanishes after tensoring with Q_p, but p-primary torsion must not be discarded in the integral version.
An isogeny inducing an isomorphism of rational representations need not induce an isomorphism of integral Tate lattices.

sources.locator: Section 3.1, Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2, printed pp. 1065--1066

Identifies the weight-two objects involved in the family application; this node specifies the actual quotient map and basepoint that the application needs.

nodes.title: Character-weighted comparison without averaging
nodes.statement: Let F/L be a finite abelian extension defining a compatible family of the preceding cycles and points, let G=Gal(F/L), and let chi:G->B^x be a character in a common coefficient field B. For the G-equivariant scalar extension gamma_* of the preceding comparison, gamma_*(sum_g chi(g) g.z)=sum_g chi(g) g.kappa_E(P). With this left-action convention each weighted sum lies in the chi^{-1}-eigenspace. No factor 1/|G| is introduced. A descent to H^1(L,V tensor chi), if used, is a further cohomological map with its own hypotheses.
hypotheses: The coefficient representations extend to G_L; this gives the quotient G-action on H^1(F,-).
The parametrization, correspondence and coefficient comparison descend to L, so gamma_* is G-equivariant.
chi is finite order and its values belong to B; it is not an unspecified algebraic Hecke character or a choice of an averaging idempotent.
proofSteps: Apply the modular-quotient comparison to every Galois conjugate.
Use linearity and equivariance to commute gamma_* with the finite weighted sum.
For h in G substitute t=hg. The coefficient chi(h^{-1}t) is chi(h)^{-1}chi(t), proving the stated eigenspace convention.
Keep the weighted sum distinct from a normalized projector. A projector requires |G| invertible in the coefficient ring, and inflation--restriction requires a separate descent argument.
acceptance: For the trivial character recover the trace, not the average.
For a cyclic group of order three and a character of order three, check that the eigenvalue is chi(h)^{-1}, not chi(h).
At p dividing |G| the unnormalized sum is integral; a claimed integral division by |G| must fail its hypothesis test.

sources.locator: Section 5.2, character specialization following equation (5.1) and Lemma 5.4
sources.match: Fixes the character-sum convention for comparison. The eigenspace calculation here is a direct reindexing argument; it does not use the problematic full symmetric-power/induction identification in Section 4.4.

nodes.title: Comparison of positive-conductor stabilized classes
nodes.statement: Let p be good ordinary for a weight-two form f of trivial character, and let alpha be the unit root of X^2-a_p X+p. Put K_n=K_{c_0 p^n} with (c_0,p)=1. For n>=1 let z_n be the rational corrected cycle class and k_n=kappa_E(P_n) its image under the compatible maps gamma_n. Then gamma_n(z_n-alpha^{-1} res(z_{n-1}))=k_n-alpha^{-1} res(k_{n-1}). This compares the p-divisible-conductor branch only. The alpha^{-n} normalization belongs to the tower, not to the definition of the unnormalized stabilized finite-level class.
hypotheses: All CM points, basepoints and coefficient identifications are compatible with the displayed field inclusions, as supplied by HE.1 and GH.1.
p splits in the imaginary quadratic field; its discriminant is less than -3, the level primes split, and p does not divide 2N phi(N), in the weight-two CH range.
Use the same scalar extension containing alpha on both sides and the restriction map of continuous cohomology.
proofSteps: Substitute r=1 in the positive-conductor branch of the geometric stabilization: p^{2r-2}/alpha becomes alpha^{-1}.
Apply the preceding quotient comparison at levels n and n-1.
Use naturality under restriction and linearity to subtract the two images. No initial-conductor formula or averaging identity is used.
acceptance: The coefficient of the lower class is alpha^{-1}, not p/alpha.
At n=1 the lower class is the raw conductor-c_0 class; this is not an invocation of an unverified conductor-zero stabilized formula.
A nonordinary alpha is rejected for integral tower normalization even though a rational finite-level linear identity can still be written.

sources.match: Provides the positive-conductor stabilization and distinguishes it from the tower normalization. No initial unit factor is silently chosen here.

nodes.title: Corestriction of the normalized positive-conductor tail
nodes.statement: In the preceding ordinary split setting, assume the actual geometric trace relation cor(k_n)=a_p k_{n-1}-res(k_{n-2}) and [K_n:K_{n-1}]=p for n>=2. Define y_n=alpha^{-n}(k_n-alpha^{-1} res(k_{n-1})) for n>=1. Then cor(y_n)=y_{n-1} for every n>=2. Consequently the positive tail has a uniquely determined bottom term y_0=cor(y_1). This does not identify that bottom term with a formula from a different normalization of Heegner classes.
hypotheses: Restriction of k_{n-2} is taken to K_{n-1} in the trace relation.
The raw trace relation and extension degree are the HE.2 geometric/ring-class results; they must not be postulated as a normalized Euler-system relation.
Corestriction after restriction acts by the extension degree. The chosen coefficient lattice contains the raw Kummer classes and alpha is a unit when integral boundedness is asserted.
proofSteps: Apply corestriction to k_n-alpha^{-1}res(k_{n-1}); obtain (a_p-p/alpha)k_{n-1}-res(k_{n-2}).
Use alpha^2-a_p alpha+p=0 to replace a_p-p/alpha by alpha.
Multiply by alpha^{-n}, obtaining alpha^{-(n-1)}(k_{n-1}-alpha^{-1}res(k_{n-2})).

Define y_0 by corestriction rather than guessing an initial Euler factor. Uniqueness of this extension of a tail follows from the single transition equation at n=1. Passage from the integral tail to the chosen Iwasawa-cohomology carrier uses GH.3's realization, not a new carrier here.
acceptance: Check n=2 explicitly; no degree-p assertion is used for K_1/K_0.
Replacing p/alpha by 1/alpha in the corestriction calculation fails the Hecke polynomial identity.
The bottom term is determined by the tail even before it is expressed through the two split Frobenius operators; the latter expression is a separate remaining comparison.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.4 and proof, printed pp. 591--593; Lemma 5.3, printed pp. 601--602
sources.match: The split recurrence is explicitly in the positive range. This node supplies the weight-two algebra of normalization in exactly that range, without claiming the printed proof also computes the missing initial split case.

nodes.title: The modular differential factor in the logarithm comparison
nodes.statement: Base change the quotient comparison to a finite unramified extension L_v/Q_p over which the curve and elliptic quotient have the good-reduction models used in BDP Section 3. Let omega_E be the chosen invariant differential and omega_f the chosen modular differential. If pi^*omega_E=c_pi omega_f, then log_{E,omega_E}(pi(x_phi)-pi(b))=c_pi AJ_dR(e_f([x_phi]-[b]))(omega_f), with the de Rham realization and f-projection transported through the same quotient. Thus replacing the Abel--Jacobi evaluation by the elliptic logarithm in a squared identity introduces c_pi^{-2}, not c_pi^{-1}. No claim that c_pi=1 or is a p-adic unit is made.
hypotheses: The local Abel--Jacobi realization and its comparison with the finite Bloch--Kato class are those of GH.1 and PadicHodgeRegulators L1; no arbitrary ramified-base extension of BDP's stated construction is inferred.
Use the actual nonzero differential-pullback scalar of the chosen parametrization.
The f-projector fixes the differential being evaluated; the projector and quotient are compatible with the de Rham realization and its pairing.
log_{E,omega_E} is the elliptic p-adic logarithm evaluated against omega_E, including its compatible extension from the formal group to the rational Kummer image.
proofSteps: Localize the rational Kummer comparison.
Apply functoriality of the Bloch--Kato logarithm and its compatibility with the elliptic formal-group logarithm.
Use adjunction of the de Rham quotient map and differential pullback to evaluate the resulting class on pi^*omega_E.
Substitute c_pi omega_f and use linearity. Squaring this equality gives the square of the scalar; cancellation requires the already specified c_pi nonzero.
acceptance: Scaling omega_E by u scales both sides by u; its square scales by u^2.
For a parametrization with c_pi=3 the squared substitution uses 1/9 rather than 1/3.
A scalar divisible by p must not preserve an integral principal ideal merely because it is invertible over Q_p.
The zero CM-power period exponent at weight two does not cancel the modular-parametrization differential scalar.

sources.locator: Sections 3.2--3.4, printed pp. 1066--1070; Introduction, printed p. 1038
sources.match: Supplies the local realization and its differential evaluation. The quotient-adjunction and scalar calculation are the comparison argument specified here, not a claim that the general period dictionary is already constructed.

nodes.title: Weight-two p-old specialization of the ordinary family
nodes.statement: Use the integral Hida branch I, critically twisted representation T-dagger, and Howard class Z_{c_0,infinity} constructed in GH.7 with Castella's author-copy normalization. Let its reference form have even weight k>2 with k congruent to 2 modulo p-1, and let nu be an arithmetic specialization of weight two and trivial character with 2 congruent to k modulo 2(p-1). Suppose its form is the ordinary p-stabilization of a newform of level prime to p. With alpha=nu(a_p), Castella's source-normalized comparison is nu(Z_{c_0,infinity})=z_{f_nu,c_0,alpha} in the identified Greenberg Iwasawa cohomology of T_{f_nu}(1). The coefficient-specialization and critical-twist identification are part of the map. This target is not an identification with every later version of the CH classes without a normalization map.
hypotheses: p does not divide 6N; c_0 is prime to pN; the imaginary quadratic discriminant is odd and less than -3; p splits.

For comparison with the CH branch, impose the classical Heegner condition that every prime dividing N splits in K; this is an explicit restricted common range, not a claim to cover all ramified-level cases in Castella.

The residual representation is p-distinguished, its restriction to G_K is irreducible, and the source's ramification condition at primes dividing (D_K,N) is retained (vacuous in the all-split common range).
Use the source's chosen lattices, ordinary filtration and arithmetic specialization map, not arbitrary isomorphic rational representations.
The weight-two p-new/multiplicative and nonordinary specializations are excluded.
proofSteps: Identify the two weight-two cycle inputs in Castella's equation (6.6) with the corrected Kummer classes through the quotient comparison, as required by Remark 6.6.
Use GH.7's moment/coefficient specialization and regulator comparison to obtain the two regulator images in equations (6.8)--(6.9), retaining their character twist and group-like factor.

Apply the global localization injectivity of Lemma 6.4 in the required weight-two extension and the local regulator injectivity cited in the proof. Equality of regulator values alone is not sufficient.

At weight two c_0^{r_nu-1}=1. Transport the equality to the fixed coefficient carrier using the explicitly constructed critical-twist map. The comparison with the 2022 CH regulator conventions is separately listed as a gap.
acceptance: A weight-two p-stabilization of a prime-to-p form is admitted; a weight-two p-new form is rejected.
Check both k congruences rather than replacing them by evenness.
Retain the finite ring-class component; the specialization is not automatically the class traced to K.
No use of injectivity of a scalar-valued regulator is permitted until the actual local and global injectivity statements have been supplied.

sources.match: The numbered theorem has weight greater than two; the following remark explicitly supplies the p-old weight-two extension and excludes the p-new case. The full proof inputs remain requests, not black-box formalized theorems.

requests.need: Supply the empty fiber-power identification at weight two, the correspondence action on the Jacobian/cohomology, and q_pi e_f=q_pi for the actual quotient. Do not use the false full symmetric-power/induction display recorded below.

Supply the degree-one Abel--Jacobi/Picard--Kummer comparison with its sign and coefficient transitions. At m=p^n, U=C minus the finite support S of a degree-zero divisor D, compare the Gysin boundary of (n_s mod m)_s in ker((Z/m)^S -> Z/m) with the Kummer boundary of [D] in J/mJ under J[m] = H^1_et(C_bar,mu_m). Use an m-division line bundle and its trivialization over U to compute the same cocycle; check signs against the source's cycle class, independence of the trivialization, Galois descent, transition in n and the actual continuous-cochain realization. A mere name AJ or a rational class is not an integral comparison. Also supply de Rham realization compatibility for the quotient.

Provide the actual CM points over their level/ring-class fields, compatible degree-zero basepoint divisors, and the map q_pi induced by the chosen modular parametrization, including the basepoint translation and field-descent identities.

Provide the raw weight-two split-conductor recurrence and degree [K_n:K_{n-1}]=p for n>=2 from the geometric/ring-class construction, with torsion/basepoint corrections actually eliminated in the stated rational image. Derive the initial split-conductor relation separately, retaining unit indices and both Frobenius operators.

Provide the abelian-variety finite and continuous p-adic Kummer maps, naturality for q_pi and restriction/corestriction, and the quotient Galois action on cohomology. The existing multiplicative Kummer map to H^1(G_K,mu_m) is not this theorem.

Identify the integral normalized tail with the existing Iwasawa-cohomology carrier and bound the cycle-to-quotient denominators uniformly. Compute its initial term before identifying it with a source formula involving u_c.

Provide the naturality of the Bloch--Kato logarithm for the Jacobian quotient and its comparison with the elliptic formal-group logarithm, including the de Rham pairing and the exact local good-reduction range.

Supply version-qualified reciprocity with actual twist, scalar and group-like-factor maps. In particular compare the t^{1-2r} pairing in Castella's family proof with the t^{-2r} pairing in the inspected 2022 CH text before transporting equalities.

Supply the Hida coefficient/critical-twist specialization, moments and regulator specializations used in equations (6.8)--(6.9), plus the precise weight-two p-old extension of Lemma 6.4 and local regulator injectivity. Decompose the cited LZ14 Proposition 4.11 input rather than assuming a scalar logarithm injective. Retain Yager-module and specialization corrections in the actual coefficient ring.

remaining: Prove and realize the finite Picard--Kummer/Gysin sign comparison and its continuous p-adic passage.
Repair or bypass the source's symmetric-power/induction display when identifying the general CM-character carrier.
Derive the initial split-conductor relation and reconcile full versus half unit-group factors between source versions and HE.8.
Construct uniform integral lattice bounds, the complete tower comparison, and the source-version regulator/twist map.
Complete the family proof's local/global injectivity prerequisites.

Construct the source-qualified consumer maps to AutomorphicCongruences L2 and RankZeroOneBSD BSD.6a without duplicating the downstream formulation comparisons owned by ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L6.

gaps.title: Degree-one realization and integral lattice
gaps.detail: The finite Picard--Kummer/Gysin comparison and transition-sign calculation are specified in the GH.1 request, not proved in a verified library here. A uniform comparison of the cycle lattice and the elliptic Tate lattice is also required before an integral system equality.

gaps.title: Symmetric-power/induction carrier
gaps.detail: The published Section 4.4 identification fails the dimension test in source issue E-GH8-1. The direct weight-two divisor/Kummer route avoids that identification. A complete comparison with the general source character construction still requires its repaired carrier and maps; the correction is not supplied by renaming the full symmetric power.

gaps.title: Initial conductor and unit normalization
gaps.detail: CH Definition 5.2 prints u_c=#O_c^x; Castella's author-copy equation (6.7) prints u_c=#O_c^x/2. This is a verified discrepancy, not by itself a proved error in either class formula. Prop. 4.4's split statement covers n>1. Compute cor(y_1) geometrically, including level descent, basepoint corrections and unit indices, then identify each convention. The positive-tail node deliberately does not claim that calculation.

gaps.title: Regulator version and injectivity comparison
gaps.detail: The inspected 2022 CH pairing has t^{-2r} and its stated sigma_{-1,p} factor, whereas the family proof uses a t^{1-2r} pairing. This needs a typed coefficient/twist comparison, not a textual replacement. The local LZ14 injectivity proof and the p-old weight-two global localization argument have not been decomposed here.

gaps.title: Main-conjecture consumer maps
gaps.detail: This packet does not identify determinant lines, characteristic ideals or primitive/imprimitive Selmer complexes. GH.8 must deliver the source-qualified cycle/point and differential maps to the consumers; ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L6 owns the general endpoint formulation comparisons. No prerequisite from an early GH.8 comparison back to that downstream endpoint is added.

sourceIssues.locator: Published Section 4.4, printed p. 593, display defining S^{r-1}(B); also present in the 2 July 2022 author revision, Section 4.4
sourceIssues.printed: S^{r-1}(B) := Sym^{2r-2} T_p(B)(1-r) tensor O_F ≃ Ind_{G_H_K}^{G_K} S^{r-1}(A) tensor O_F.
sourceIssues.correction: Do not identify the full ordinary symmetric power with the induced symmetric power. For positive degree the direct sum of the pure symmetric powers of the conjugate Tate modules is the relevant induced submodule; mixed monomials remain in the full symmetric power. In degree zero the full symmetric power is one-dimensional and needs a separate treatment. A repaired CM-character carrier and its maps must be constructed; simply changing the notation does not supply them.
sourceIssues.reason: Put h=[H_K:K] and extend scalars to a characteristic-zero coefficient field. T_p(B) has dimension 2h. At r=1 the left side has dimension 1 and the right side dimension h, so the displayed isomorphism is impossible when h>1. At r=2 their dimensions are h(2h+1) and 3h, again unequal for h>1. Tate twisting and coefficient extension do not change these dimensions. This refutes the display, not automatically all later theorems.
